title: Forging and Passing or Attempting to Pass: Two Theories in One Count

source.release: 2026 Criminal Jury Instructions (as adopted by the Judicial Council, February 2026)

body: The defendant is charged [in Count ______] with forgery of [a/an] ______ <insert type[s] of document[s] from Pen. Code, § 470(d)>.

The defendant is being prosecuted for forgery under two theories: (1) that the defendant forged the document; and (2) that the defendant (passed[,]/used[,]/[or] (attempted/[or] offered) to use) the forged document.
Each theory of forgery has different requirements, and I have instructed you on both.

You may not find the defendant guilty of forgery unless all of you agree that the People have proved that the defendant committed forgery under at least one theory. But all of you do not have to agree on the same theory.

bench_notes.text: This instruction is to be given when the prosecution pursues the two theories of forgery of a single document in one count. (See *People v. Sutherland* (1993) 17 Cal.App.4th 602, 618–619 [21 Cal.Rptr.2d 752].)

authority.text: • Unanimity on Theory Not Required. *People v. Sutherland* (1993) 17 Cal.App.4th 602, 618–619 [21 Cal.Rptr.2d 752].
